chunks: And this report was narrated by Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Nasr and Ali ibn al-Hakam and al-Hasan ibn Ali al-Washsha from Aban ibn Uthman from Razin, the seller of fabrics, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said:

I said to him: 'A slave woman is with me, and I have sexual relations with her, then she dies or leaves my ownership, and I then marry her daughter. Is it permissible for me to have sexual relations with her?' He said: 'Yes, there is no harm in it. Allah only forbade this from the free women (al-hara'ir), but as for the slave women, there is no harm in it.'

The first point in this report is that it is rare and unique (shadh), and it was not narrated by anyone other than the seller of fabrics (Razin), even though it has repeated in the books. And what follows this pattern among the rare narrations must be discarded and not used as a counter-argument against the numerous hadiths. Furthermore, it has been narrated what breaks this narration and agrees with what we presented earlier. So if the matter is as we mentioned, it is obligatory to follow the narration that agrees with the other narrations and to turn away from the narration that he alone narrated, because it is possible that it was a mistake (wahm).
ai.seo_question: Is it permissible to marry the daughter of a slave woman you previously owned and had relations with?
ai.summary: Shaykh al-Tusi records this narration from Imam al-Baqir (AS) establishing the permissibility of marrying the daughter of one's own slave woman after her death or release, distinguishing this case from the prohibition on free women. However, the scholar classifies this report as *shadh* (rare/unique) because it is transmitted solely through Razin al-Bayyag al-Anmat, leading him to set it aside in favor of more widely attested narrations that align with general juristic consensus.
